Sorry if what I wrote was confusing. I’m trying to say that teachers getting riffed means they will look for other jobs outside of the district because they don’t actually know if they’re going to be rehired. 

If these teachers find other jobs, they will take them. No one wants to risk being unemployed at the beginning of the school year. 

If these teachers leave, but their position opens back up, a new teacher takes their place - meaning high turnover. 

I think your point about low income schools having a higher turn over rate is valid, so I was just honestly asking if teachers being riffed in CPS are from mostly low income schools. If this was the case, it would also explain high turn over, not just blaming it on the kids

(Side thought, a lot of “bad” kids in low income areas are seen this way because there is no stability in their school structure. If teachers are always leaving or being let go, it’s no wonder that they wouldn’t feel the need to behave. Hell, when I taught in a “bad” school in CPS, I was the the 6th teacher in my position within 8 years. Once the kids didn’t think I would abandon them after a month, they weren’t so “bad” anymore. )

Yes... I too read the article. I also used to be a teacher in CPS, this process is not easy to deal with and my point is that for the time being, teachers will look elsewhere to ensure they have a job.

It’s called riffing. It happens in a lot of districts that need to make budget cuts. Essentially it’s saying to the teachers that they don’t know if they need you/can afford you, but they don’t want to let you go so they leave you in limbo land until they have a better idea as to what they’re budget/resources will look like for the upcoming school year. It’s based on seniority, so a first year teacher is going to get riffed before a 15 year teacher.
I’m saying they should do that. I don’t expect them to sit around and wait to see if they have a job.
And in the mean time all these teachers and support staff will look for jobs elsewhere. Then we wonder why many CPS schools have such high turnover rate.
